scope: The SET COVERING decision problem is NP-complete: given a finite family of finite sets and a positive integer k, decide whether at most k members cover the union of the entire family, with standard explicit finite encodings and binary integer parameters.
boundary: Main Theorem and problem6, printed p.94; completeness/reduction definitions pp.88,93, encoding discussion p.89, NP membership p.97, NODE COVER reduction p.98. An explicit-universe formulation is an adaptation: require every member to be a subset of the universe; uncovered universe elements are immediate negative cases. k=0 is a trivial additional case. No approximability result, proof that P differs from NP, or universal sensor-selection hardness follows. A project sensor encoding must exhibit its own polynomial reduction; unrestricted scalar basis selection is a different problem.
limitations: Explicit-universe and zero-budget cases are adaptations.
No private vault used; knowledge adapter extension, not unrelated corpus expansion.
